messages.subject: Question on mod indices suggestion
parts:
Hi all,

I've used mod indices a bit. The first three here don't really make sense, and for the fourth, though I get that here the mod indices are suggesting regressing social lifestyle on age, I don't get what that means with regard to implementation in my model. Is it suggesting that I create a new regression with sl as the endogenous variable with one exogenous variable of age?

Thanks much!

James

> modindices(fit.latent.separate_trauma_res_model.3, sort. = TRUE, minimum.value = 10)
                      lhs op                rhs                     mi    epc sepc.lv
215                   age  ~       neglectscore    42.781  0.333   0.333
214                   age  ~         abusescore    40.059  0.321   0.321
210                   age  ~                 sl              32.826 -0.329  -0.329
189                    sl  ~                age               27.972 -0.310  -0.310

Similarly, here is it suggesting what I write above, or is it suggesting that neglect score be put into the latent variable of sl?
165           sl  ~          neglectscore 78.967 -0.533  -0.533

This is the model:
fit.latent_trauma_separate_res.3 <- '#factor loadings; measurement model portion
pl =~ exercisescore + mindfulnessscore + promistscore
sl =~ family_support + friendshipcount + friendshipnet  

#regressions: structural model
emotionalsupportscore ~ sl + gender
resiliencescore ~ age + sesscore + emotionalsupportscore + sl + tr* exposure + ind_ab * abusescore + ind_neg * neglectscore

wellbeing ~ age + gender + ethnicity + sesscore + dir_rs* resiliencescore + dir_tr*exposure + pl + emotionalsupportscore + sl + abusescore + neglectscore

neglectscore ~~ abusescore
'

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Question on mod indices suggestion
parts: The first three here don't really make sense, and for the fourth, though I get that here the mod indices are suggesting regressing social lifestyle on age, I don't get what that means with regard to implementation in my model. Is it suggesting that I create a new regression with sl as the endogenous variable with one exogenous variable of age?

Modification indices are not guaranteed to make sense.  I would recommend only paying attention to ones for parameters you would consider a priori, even using lavTestScore() instead to explicitly request score tests for specific constrained parameters.

Because you have both latent and observed predictors, I would recommend treating the observed ones as single-indicator factors, so that their covariances with latent exogenous variables are already estimated by default (as they should be).  Then those silly indices will not pop up.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Question on mod indices suggestion
parts: can you clarify what you mean by single indicator factors

For  example, pull age into the latent space:

AGE =~ 1*age
AGE ~~ NA*AGE
age ~~ 0*age

Then replace "age" with "AGE" in the regression models in your syntax.

This means either treating some clearly nominal variables as continuous (gender, ethnicity),  or treating them as ordinal indicators (an arbitrary distinction when binary) using the ordered= argument.  The latter option requires more constraints:

AGE =~ 1*age
AGE ~~ 1*AGE # because the residual variances would have been fixed to 1 
age ~~ 0*age

and setting parameterization = "theta"

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
James,
Terrence described two alternative procedures, one that treated the variables as continuous, one that treated them as ordinal.  However, your code (e.g., ethnicity) appears to blend elements of each procedure.  As Terrence noted, the treating a variable as ordinal requires more constraints, so one would expect this mixing to lead to under-identification in the model.  Caveat:  I do not use the convenience functions like sem() and could therefore be missing something.  However, if I am correct, you need to adjust the code for variables that you treat as ordinal to match Terrence's example for that procedure, following the second example in his message.

Keith

John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus
Frontiers of Test Validity Theory: Measurement, Causation and Meaning.
http://www.routledge.com/books/details/9781841692203/

Terrence described two alternative procedures, one that treated the variables as continuous, one that treated them as ordinal.  However, your code (e.g., ethnicity) appears to blend elements of each procedure.  As Terrence noted, the treating a variable as ordinal requires more constraints, so one would expect this mixing to lead to under-identification in the model.  Caveat:  I do not use the convenience functions like sem() and could therefore be missing something.  However, if I am correct, you need to adjust the code for variables that you treat as ordinal to match Terrence's example for that procedure, following the second example in his message.

On Wed, Apr 28, 2021 at 9:13 PM Terrence Jorgensen <tjorge...@gmail.com> wrote:
can you clarify what you mean by single indicator factors

For  example, pull age into the latent space:

AGE =~ 1*age
AGE ~~ NA*AGE
age ~~ 0*age

Then replace "age" with "AGE" in the regression models in your syntax.

This means either treating some clearly nominal variables as continuous (gender, ethnicity),  or treating them as ordinal indicators (an arbitrary distinction when binary) using the ordered= argument.  The latter option requires more constraints:

AGE =~ 1*age
AGE ~~ 1*AGE # because the residual variances would have been fixed to 1 
age ~~ 0*age

and setting parameterization = "theta"
